title: Fuzzy topological analysis of fuzzy Helm graphs with applications to protein interaction networks.
authors: Mufti, Zeeshan Saleem; Tedjani, Ali H; Liaqat, Shama; Ganati, Gamachu Adugna
one_liner_zh: 该文对模糊Helm图进行模糊拓扑指数分析并应用于P53蛋白互作网络，虽涉及蛋白互作网络但非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，仅属图论网络分析，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: In biological and chemical networks, in which the strength of interactions is often not absolute, uncertainty is an inherent feature of many real-world networks. A fuzzy graph consists of vertices with fuzzy memberships and fuzzy relationships among vertices and edges; therefore, fuzzy graph theory is a natural approach for modelling systems in which the connections between the vertices are fuzzy or not precisely known. Helm graphs are constructed by adding pendant vertices to the outer cycle of a wheel graph and have a layered hierarchy similar to that found in hub-and-spoke networks, such as those of protein interaction and communication networks. Encouraged by this structural similarity, in the present study, some degree-based fuzzy topological indices are investigated on fuzzy Helms graphs. Specifically, we obtain closed-form analytical expressions for the fuzzy Zagreb, fuzzy Randic, fuzzy Harmonic, fuzzy F-index, fuzzy Sombor, fuzzy Misbalance Prodeg, and fuzzy Nirmala indices. The formulas are derived directly from the partition of the type of vertices of the fuzzy Helm graph and are checked symbolically and by a numerical example. The deduced expressions show the dependence of these descriptors on structural properties, such as pendant attachments, edge weight distribution, and connectivity of the hubs. As a concrete application, the proposed framework is used in the case of the P53 protein interaction network, a central pathway in cancer biology. The numerical results illustrate the ability of fuzzy descriptors to differentiate between the dominant regulatory role of P53 and the role played by interacting partners, which cannot be achieved by classical crisp indices because they lose the graded aspect of biological interaction confidence. Therefore, this study suggests the use of fuzzy topological indices for network analysis in a wider context and suggests the natural development of the said approach to other families of fuzzy graphs, as well as to uncertain networks in chemical and biological applications.
abstract_zh: 在生物和化学网络中，相互作用的强度往往并非绝对，不确定性是许多现实世界网络的固有特征。模糊图由具有模糊隶属度的顶点及顶点与边之间的模糊关系构成；因此，模糊图论是建模顶点间连接模糊或不完全精确系统的自然方法。Helm图通过在轮图的外环上添加悬挂顶点构建，其分层结构与枢纽-辐条网络（如蛋白质相互作用和通信网络）相似。受此结构相似性的启发，本研究探讨了模糊Helm图上若干基于度的模糊拓扑指数。具体而言，我们获得了模糊Zagreb、模糊Randic、模糊Harmonic、模糊F指数、模糊Sombor、模糊Misbalance Prodeg和模糊Nirmala指数的闭式解析表达式。这些公式直接基于模糊Helm图顶点类型的划分推导，并通过符号验证及数值示例进行检验。推导出的表达式展示了这些描述符对结构属性（如悬挂连接、边权重分布和枢纽连通性）的依赖性。作为具体应用，所提出的框架被用于P53蛋白质相互作用网络（癌症生物学中的核心通路）案例。数值结果表明，模糊描述符能够区分P53的主导调控作用与其相互作用伙伴所扮演的角色，而经典清晰指数因丧失生物相互作用置信度的分级特性而无法实现这一点。因此，本研究建议在更广泛背景下使用模糊拓扑指数进行网络分析，并自然推动该方法向其他模糊图族及化学和生物应用中不确定网络的拓展。
